findings.reasoning: With keysAway==='busy', the inText exemption can never apply because 16807 conditions it on keysAway === 'window'; the !editorUndo is false only for keysAway==='window' too. So EVERY key - including keys typed into a visible fastaInput - returns at 16818 before flow can reach 16849-16851's loadButton click or any branch of 16830-17090. The user CAN keep typing into the Input box during a job: handleKeyDown only preventDefaults modifier shortcuts (16813, inside the 16812 test that lets /^[cvxafp]$/ and pure modifier keys pass), so plain characters still reach the textarea natively; ctrl combinations get the toast at 16814 ('Wait until the running job is done (or press Stop): the alignment cannot be changed meanwhile.'). This does not matter for state: the drafted text is inert until the user explicitly clicks Load after the job, and _mafftAlignWithUi (script.js 26143-26157) fingerprints state.seqs before/after the run so a Load landing mid-run is caught rather than overwriting the result. Covered.
findings.scenario: Job running (busy overlay), focus already in the Input box: user types residues - browser inserts them (harmless draft); presses Ctrl+L expecting Load - gets the 'Wait until the running job is done' toast instead of 16850's click, so state.seqs and state.deletedHistory cannot be touched from the keyboard during a run.
findings.title: ok: keysAway==='busy' returns at 16818 for all keys including textarea focus - typing in fastaInput stays native and cannot change state

findings.reasoning: When keysAway==='window' (Sequence editor is a blocking dialog) and focus is in a visible text field inside it, inText is true so the guard lets the event through; the only alignment branches then reachable are case 'z' (16923-16931) and case 'y' (16932-16936), both of which first test _seqEditOpen() (16927 'if (_seqEditOpen()) { if (e.shiftKey) _seqEditRedo(); else _seqEditUndo(); }', 16933 'if (_seqEditOpen()) _seqEditRedo();') and thus route to the editor's own undo/redo, which edits the textarea, not state.seqs. If focus is instead in a name field or the sequence textarea, keys are returned at 16853/16864 anyway. Covered.
findings.scenario: Sequence editor dialog open, focus anywhere inside it, Ctrl+Z: the editor's text undo runs (editorUndo at 16806 exempted exactly this); with focus in a text field, 16859/16853 return before the switch, so no alignment/history change. Covered.
findings.title: ok: with the Sequence editor open, Ctrl+Z/Ctrl+Y reach only _seqEditUndo/_seqEditRedo, which cannot corrupt the alignment

findings.reasoning: This same line also shows the failure mode of findings 1-2 from the opposite side: case 'z' deliberately checks _seqEditOpen() first because a blanket undo action while keysAway==='window' would corrupt state - proving the authors accepted the premise. But no other case of the 16902 switch, and none of the modified-arrow branches, performs any _isTextEntry or _seqEditOpen or activeElement check; their only protection is the fast-path exit at 16853/16864, which line 16846 fails to give a focused <select>. Net answer to the question: for TEXTAREA and single-line INPUT fields inside a window, NO branch of 16830-17090 can change state.seqs / selection / undo (16827-16831 skips via typing check, 16849-16853 returns except the fastaInput Ctrl+L load, 16859-16864 returns); the only lever that reaches the mutation switch under keysAway==='window' is a focused <select>, plus the unconfirmed Load at 16850.
findings.scenario: Any keyboard action from a window select or from the Input-box Ctrl+L while a window is open is unguarded; from every other field the case is covered.
findings.title: Only the editor provices a pattern check before acting; the remaining switch cases rely entirely on the fast-path exits that a <select> misses

note: Q1 part 2 summary. With keysAway==='window' and focus in a visible text field inside the window, the guard (16807) lets the event run the full body. For TEXTAREAs, 16848-16853 returns for all keys except line 16850's Ctrl+L in fastaInput, which clicks Load with NO ask-first confirmation (v332 added the confirmation only for Ctrl+L outside text fields; I could not verify whether the Load button handler itself confirms). For single-line INPUTs, 16859-16864 returns everything except searchInput's Ctrl+F (harmless). Ctrl+D checks _isTextEntry (16831) and is safe. The real hole: _isTextEntry counts a <select> as text entry (so a visible focused drop-down in dotPlotModal / repeatFinderModal / treeBuilderModal - index.html 1241, 1371, 1451 - is exempt from the window guard), but isFormField at 16846 omits SELECT, so the select falls past the fast-path into the full switch at 16902+, where Ctrl+R/Ctrl+Delete/Ctrl+Z/Ctrl+Y/Ctrl+B/Ctrl+U and the modified-arrow row moves mutate state.seqs, the selection and the undo history with no _isTextEntry check of their own. The Sequence editor's Ctrl+Z/Y are correctly diverted to _seqEditUndo/_seqEditRedo (line 16927). Busy case: inText is not consulted when keysAway==='busy' (16807 conditions it on 'window'), so 16818 returns for every key; the user can still type into fastaInput natively (only modifier shortcuts are preventDefaulted), but nothing in 16830-17090 is reachable during a job - typing is an inert draft, Ctrl+L gets the toast at 16814, and _mafftAlignWithUi's fingerprint check is a second line of defense.
